Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We propose a $32 million class fund distributed automatically to all identified members, with $6 million in separate attorneys’ fees and expenses subject to court approval. Any fees the court does not award would go to the class, not Brightline. We believe these terms provide meaningful, direct relief while accounting for the risks and delay of continued litigation.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate the focus on direct, automatic payments and agree that unawarded fees should benefit the class. Given the unresolved certification and merits risks, Brightline proposes a $26 million class fund plus up to $5 million in court-approved fees and expenses, without clear sailing.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate Brightline’s agreement to automatic payments and to directing any unawarded fees to the class. To better reflect the scale of the renewal charges while accounting for litigation risk, we propose a $30 million class fund and $5.5 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses, with the other protections unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We appreciate your movement and agree on automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and directing any unawarded fees to the class. In light of the remaining certification and merits risks, Brightline can offer a $28 million class fund and $5.25 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: plaintiff
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: We are close. If Brightline can increase the class fund to $29 million, we will accept its proposed $5.25 million in separately paid, court-approved fees and expenses. Automatic payments, no clear sailing, and directing any unawarded fees to the class would remain unchanged.

Hargrove Lane LLP.speaker: defense
Hargrove Lane LLP.message: Brightline accepts your latest term sheet: a $29 million class fund with automatic distribution, $5.25 million in separately paid fees and expenses subject to court approval, no clear sailing, and any unawarded fees going to the class. We look forward to documenting the agreement for court approval.

private_notes.private_reasoning: Open with a substantial class recovery that reflects the litigation risk and delay. Because every member is identifiable, insist on automatic payments and no reversion of unawarded fees to Brightline. Keep the fee request separate and subject to court approval.

Their $38 million proposal is within the $40 million limit and has court-approval-friendly terms, but there is room to negotiate a lower total outlay. Counter with automatic distribution and no fee reversion or clear sailing.

The defense offer provides substantial automatic relief, but there is room to negotiate a higher class recovery. Keep the protections that unawarded fees benefit the class and that payments are automatic. A moderate counteroffer recognizes certification and trial risks without trading class relief for fees.

Counsel’s $35.5 million proposal is within authority and offers direct class relief, but there is room to negotiate a lower total cash outlay. Counter at $33.25 million while preserving the approval-friendly terms.

The $28 million automatic-distribution fund is already substantial relative to the risk-adjusted trial outcome, particularly given certification risk and delay. A modest counter focused solely on class relief may secure an additional $1 million without jeopardizing agreement; the proposed fee remains subject to court approval, with any reduction benefiting the class.

The $34.25 million total is within authorization. Automatic distribution, no clear sailing, and class receipt of unawarded fees support approval. The remaining $1 million difference in the class fund is modest relative to litigation risk and cost; accept.

declaration.negotiation_history_statement: The settlement resulted from arm’s-length negotiations with defense counsel. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were discussed during the same negotiations; fees were not deferred until after class relief was agreed. The agreement provides a $29 million class fund distributed automatically to identified class members, plus up to $5.25 million in separately paid fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request, and any amount the Court declines to award will go to the class rather than revert to Brightline.
